name: B10-0079/2024 (PPE) – The democratic backsliding and threats to political pluralism in Georgia
title: Resolution on the democratic backsliding and threats to political pluralism in Georgia
part_text:
The European Parliament asks the European Union to act on Georgia. It wants the European Union to consider suspending visa-free travel for Georgians if the October 2024 election is not fair. It calls for personal sanctions on Bidzina Ivanishvili and other officials accused of undermining democracy. It also asks Georgia to cancel two new laws, one on foreign-funded groups and one on family values and minors, and to return to a pro-European path.

- The European Union may suspend visa-free travel for Georgians if the election fails international standards.
- Sanctions are proposed for Ivanishvili and officials blamed for backsliding; the United States has already acted.
- Georgia is asked to cancel the two laws and free former President Mikheil Saakashvili; the Parliament only recommends, so the Council and European Union countries decide.
